historia:
SurePayroll tasked Farco Studio with redesigning their Business Online Payroll platform to create a white-label solution for 21 bank partners. Each microsite required unique branding, including color palettes, logos, and content. We collaborated as part of Farco's Webflow development team to build a scalable CMS system that streamlined customization for these microsites. The result was a flexible, user-friendly platform that ensured brand consistency while meeting the individual needs of each partner.

CMS Structuring: Dynamism and Scalability

We designed a system based on Webflow's CMS that allowed us to manage all the information and customization needed for each bank. These were the key collections we created:

  • Bank Microsites: to generate the main page for each bank.
  • Refer a Client: a form for referring clients.
  • Thank You Pages: two collections for the thank-you pages after form submissions (referrals and contact).
  • Privacy Policy and Terms of Use: legal content customized for each bank.
  • Benefits: to highlight the benefits of the services in the second section of the main page.‍
  • FAQs: dynamic information for the pricing section.

This is how we built the sitemap for all the dynamic pages, interconnected through references and multi-references, creating a tailored experience for each bank's users.

Dynamic Branding: Variables and Scalable Nomenclature

The key to deploying each bank's specific branding was establishing a system based on dynamic variables connected to CMS fields. We defined a common root with variables corresponding to primary and secondary colors, which were then called through classes in Webflow using a standardized and consistent naming convention.

This approach allowed us to:

  1. Maintain design consistency across all pages.
  2. Easily scale to new banks by replicating the system without altering its core structure.
  3. Ensure swift and precise implementation of branding elements.
Result: A Flexible and Adaptable System

Thanks to this white-label structure integrated with Webflow's CMS, we developed a system that ensures an experience tailored to each bank's needs while maintaining full scalability. This dynamic approach allows SurePayroll to expand its network of banks without compromising quality or visual consistency.

descripcion: The redesign of EndoAula focused on aligning the platform with the new identity of EndoAula Conecta. This process involved creating a fresh and modern image that reflected both the professionalism of the medical content and the accessibility and functionality characteristic of a subscription-based learning platform.

EndoAulaConecta is a subscription-based platform offering educational video content on endoscopies, led by Joaquín, a renowned physician. Using Webflow, MemberStack, Stripe, and Vimeo, we developed a scalable and autonomous solution that gained hundreds of subscribers within weeks, recovering its initial investment in under 4 months. The platform is now expanding with new courses, showcasing the potential of no-code for specialized niches.
historia:
The no-code revolution is enabling the creation of digital products in markets that previously couldn’t afford them, leading to valuable projects in highly specific niches. This is the story of how we created the Netflix for endoscopists.

A few months ago, Joaquín, a leading physician at Madrid’s Hospital 12 de Octubre and CEO of EndoAula, approached us with an exciting challenge. He had built a loyal following on YouTube by creating valuable educational content about endoscopies. While his community and video engagement continued to grow, the economic value didn’t match up. His proposal? To create a subscription-based platform where users could access a catalog of videos on how to perform endoscopies, essentially, a "Netflix for endoscopists."

Design & Development with No-Code

With the concept in hand, we explored viable no-code solutions using Webflow. Our chosen stack consisted of:

  • MemberStack for managing user creation and subscriptions, paired with Stripe for reliable recurring payments.
  • Plyr.io to design a custom video player matching the platform’s identity.
  • Vimeo for video hosting, ensuring seamless playback.

This no-code stack provided the flexibility to build an entirely independent platform with a tailored design. The result? A platform that is visually engaging, functional, and easy for Joaquín’s team to manage autonomously via Webflow’s CMS. They can now add, edit, or remove videos effortlessly while customizing the platform’s structure.

Key Features
  • Subscription Management: MemberStack + Stripe ensures smooth account creation, password recovery, and subscription handling.
  • Custom Video Player: Designed with Plyr.io to enhance user experience.
  • Scalable CMS: Capable of managing up to 9,000 videos hosted on Vimeo.
Results

The project was delivered in 4 months with an investment of under €10,000. Thanks to an effective launch strategy, the platform quickly gained hundreds of satisfied subscribers, impressed with both the content and usability.

Technically, the no-code setup has proven robust, with AWS-powered Webflow servers handling the load seamlessly. The platform is already profitable, and new features like courses are being added by reusing components.

This success story not only highlights the possibilities of no-code for niche industries but also inspires others to create independent educational platforms like this.

historia:
We worked together with the research center MIK at Mondragon University to fully digitalize their triple-impact evaluation tool. The main challenge of this project was to create a custom, multi-step questionnaire that would allow any company to easily assess its environmental, social and governance performance. The final result is displayed visually on the web, and a PDF is automatically generated and sent by email, making the experience complete from start to finish.

In addition to all the functional logic, we handled the full design of the landing page as well as the entire user experience of both the questionnaire and the results interface. We designed the charts, the indicators and the step-by-step interactions, creating a clean, aesthetic and fully responsive interface. The whole visual system adheres to MIK Mondragon’s brand identity and to the guidelines provided by their team, ensuring coherence, accessibility and a smooth experience throughout.

For the multi-step form we used Formly, which allowed us to build a structured flow fully aligned with MIK’s methodology.

This enables each user to move through the questionnaire step by step, completing each block while their responses are encoded directly in the URL via urlParams.

On the results page, the system reads the parameters included in the URL and automatically cross-references them with the data stored in Google Sheets, where all benchmarks and sector averages are kept. From there, Google App Scripts processes all the information and performs the necessary calculations. Finally, the full report is rendered, including bar charts, color-coded percentage indicators and sector comparisons that allow the user to instantly understand where their company stands in each triple-impact category.

To complete the experience we used Printable.js to generate the PDF. Its role is to capture the fully rendered HTML, prepare it for printing and send it to a serverless function hosted on Vercel. The function then connects to Resend, which sends the PDF to the user as an email attachment, closing a fully automated flow with no manual intervention.

Throughout the entire development process, we used Cursor AI to help generate the JS files that were ultimately deployed on Netlify.

The end result is a robust and fully digitalized tool capable of guiding any company through the ESG assessment process, presenting clear and visually engaging results, and delivering a professional report in just seconds. An end-to-end experience that combines methodology, design and technology to make a complex process feel simple.

historia:
Working with Invopop was a pleasure for us, largely thanks to collaborating closely with Juan Moliner, Invopop’s co-founder. His boundless energy and creativity took us to the next level. Our main objectives focused on enhancing the design of specific pages and components to enrich the user experience and managing the CMS with over 100 items in Webflow. We implemented multiple references across collections and connected it to Notion as the primary database through WhaleSync.

Design Enhancements

For Invopop’s design, we focused on creating user-friendly pages that enhance both clarity and navigation. Key pages include the Countries Coverage page, the Invoicing Guides with interactive map, and a specific Coverage Tech page, each tailored to make complex content more accessible. Our design improvements aligns with Invopop’s visual identity, presenting information in a approachable way while supporting an easy-to-navigate user experience.

From Notion to Webflow with WhaleSync

Our integration between Notion and Webflow was highly granular. We created a fully automated CMS structure. We set up a process where Notion serves as the primary database, allowing the client to update data directly. Thanks to WhaleSync, each CMS item is synchronized with its respective fields. This enables components like customer success stories, local electronic invoicing costs, and country-specific data to be updated seamlessly. Everything syncs automatically, allowing the website to reflect new data dynamically with minimal manual effort from the Invopop team in Notion. This solution helps Invopop focus on what truly matters without the hassle of managing Webflow.

Interactive global map with SVGs from CMS

The interactive map we built is a feature we're particularly proud of. Each country on the map is set up as a CMS item, connected to Notion, and contains specific information like billing coverage status and regulations. SVG paths and XY coordinates allow for precise placement, while filtering options enable users to navigate by tags such as B2B, B2C, or B2G billing capabilities. The map’s interactive features, like hover animations and overlays, create an immersive experience for users exploring global billing regulations. With this CMS-driven approach, the map is both scalable and easily to update.

Multi-language with Webflow Localization

Using Webflow's localization feature, we translated all pages and CMS items from English to Spanish. Although the process was complex and largely manual, it allowed Invopop’s content to be SEO-friendly in both languages, paving the way for brand internationalization.

Conclusion

We transformed Invopop’s website into a user-centered platform, supported by a solid CMS foundation that can scale as Invopop grows. Through this project, we deepened our ability to develop interactive components that align aesthetically with the visual identity, as well as building a scalable website thanks to the CMS integrated with Notion with WhaleSync. Additionally, we adapted seamlessly to Invopop’s workflow, using Slack for communication and delivering tasks on-demand to ensure smooth collaboration and efficient project management.

historia:
A few months ago, José Luis Antúnez introduced us to Pablo, the CEO of Numen Games, who leads a project aimed at transforming how we interact with the Internet. His vision is ambitious: to turn the web into a 3D virtual environment where experiences are so immersive that you can "feel" what you see on the screen. Even in its early stages, they are already creating experiences for companies that help sustain this powerful vision of the future.

The challenge was clear: Numen's website did not reflect the potential of their project. Our task was to showcase the innovation, ambition, and culture of Numen Games based on their newly established visual identity.

Starting point:
The Process: Immersion and Narrative Strategy

We started with an in-depth meeting with Pablo to understand their new narrative strategy. This is a crucial part of every project, as we need to dive deeply into each one to truly understand what is needed. This work often goes unnoticed because it’s pure analysis, but when done right, it’s evident in the final result.

We defined a clear direction:

  • Convey the 3D focus.
  • Represent the gaming culture behind Numen.
  • Reflect their ambition to change the world of the internet.
  • Showcase transparency as a core value.
From Ideas to Design

With this in mind, we started structuring the Figma file. We always follow the same structure to ensure the project’s success:

  1. Structure: Sketch the website’s sitemap and the sections of each page without design.
  2. Web Look & Feel: Present different visual style options for the client to choose their preferred direction.
  3. Web Screens & Development: Once the visual style is decided, design all pages and mark them for development. This streamlines timelines.
  4. Library: Define colors, typography, buttons, and graphic resources, everything needed for a coherent and consistent project.

Thanks to the extensive branding materials Pablo provided, we started by defining the library to establish a solid foundation.

Structuring the New Website

Before diving into defining the visual aesthetics, we sketched the new sitemap for Numen and the structure of the homepage. The goal: guide users to the contact form and encourage them to try a 3D demo.

Look & Feel: Our Favorite Phase

This is the stage where we play with all the information gathered to convey it visually.

These were the different proposals we presented during the first delivery:

Of the five proposals, they loved the first one, which was also our favorite. The idea behind this proposal was to represent the gateway to the 3D world offered by Numen, animating doors as if you had to pass through them to enter Numen.

With the visual style chosen, we began designing and structuring all the pages.
‍

Designing and Iterating all pages

We moved on to the iteration phase, a critical moment where the design fully comes to life. This process involved designing and refining the nine main pages of the project: Home, Services, Blog, Manifesto, Contact, Numinia, Help Center, Pricing, and Team.

During this stage, we worked collaboratively with the Numen team, ensuring that every page reflected their vision and met their strategic objectives. Each week, we updated the Figma file with the progress made, keeping the client informed and providing space for continuous feedback.

The iteration process allowed us to adjust and improve every detail, from structure to visual elements and usability. In this case, we focused on:

  • Aligning the narrative of each page with the project’s overall storytelling.
  • Maintaining visual consistency across all elements to convey a strong identity.
  • Optimizing the user experience, prioritizing intuitive navigation and conversions to key objectives like the contact form and 3D demo.

This iterative approach not only ensures high-quality results but also fosters constant collaboration, turning the client into a creative director.
‍

The result

The redesign of Numen Games resulted in a digital experience that harmoniously combines aesthetics and functionality. Each page is designed to convey their essence: the ambition to revolutionize the internet and connect on a human level through 3D.

Visually, the website stands out for:

  • Impactful typography that balances modernity and clarity, reinforcing the brand’s authority and ambition.
  • An immersive color palette, carefully selected to evoke a futuristic and professional atmosphere while maintaining the warmth of its gaming identity.
  • Dynamic interactions that create an immersive experience, guiding the user through a smooth and engaging journey.
  • Subtle yet prominent 3D elements, strategically integrated to reinforce the narrative without overwhelming the user.

Structurally, the design prioritizes intuitive navigation and conversion objectives. From the homepage to specific pages like services or contact, the visual hierarchy and element placement lead users toward key actions, such as exploring the 3D demo or initiating a conversation with Numen’s team.

As a whole, the website not only represents Numen’s vision but also acts as a gateway to the future of the internet they are building. Both Pablo and his team were thrilled with the outcome.

The Future

We are currently working on documenting Numen’s Figma in detail to release it as open-source, enabling anyone to build Numen.

Gracias a la estrecha colaboración con Nuria y su equipo, pudimos crear una página web que refleja fielmente el trabajo y el compromiso de Vitalera para transformar la atención médica digital.

resena.texto: Trabajar con Treseiscero ha sido una gran decisión. El equipo pudo transmitir lo que hace nuestra tecnología. Ha sido un placer y el equipo es el mejor que he visto en diseño y servicio al cliente.

descripcion: Logramos desarrollar un concepto que transmitiese accesibilidad para guiar a los estudiantes en su futuro profesional. descripcion: We migrated Remerge’s website from Craft CMS to Webflow, rebuilding the entire component architecture from scratch, implementing multilingual support across 4 languages, and migrating 350+ CMS items and static pages into a scalable system for their marketing team.

resena.texto: Working with the treseiscero team on our website migration was a great experience from start to finish. They handled a complex project with multilingual support, custom component architecture and a large content migration with solid precision.

historia:
The Remerge project was a major challenge. One of those migrations where every detail matters, requiring careful validation and many hours making sure everything was exactly where it needed to be.

The challenge was to migrate the entire website from Craft CMS to Webflow, working directly from the code inspector and handling multilingual support across 4 languages:

🇺🇸 EN, English
🇰🇷 KR, 한국어
🇯🇵 JP, 日本語
🇨🇳 CN, 中文

We worked directly from the original website, inspecting the code and rebuilding the entire architecture from scratch. From the style variables and spacing system library, to creating every component in a way that allowed the marketing team to easily reuse and scale them in the future.

Over the course of 2 months, we developed more than 30 static pages, alongside a CMS with 2 main collections and more than 350 items. And yes, validating all of that takes a huge amount of time.

Even while using Cursor + Webflow MCP, we still had to manually review almost every piece of content across all 4 languages to ensure everything had been migrated correctly. AI was certainly helpful, but there were still countless details that required manual review to make sure everything was perfect.

This project was a big challenge successfully overcome, and it gives us even more confidence to take on complex migrations and large-scale projects in the future.

A huge thank you to Fred Simmons and Guilherme Escobar for the trust. It was a pleasure working closely together throughout the entire process.

descripcion: Full Webflow redesign and development for Cubbo, bringing the Mexico and Brazil projects together into a single localized website, componentized and ready to scale.

resena.texto: We loved working with Andoni and Eric. The result exceeded our expectations, but the best part of the experience was how incredibly proactive they were. I never had to chase them at any point they came to me with proactive solutions. From day one, they understood exactly who we were, what we do, and what we needed, and they ran with it.

historia:
Working with Cubbo was smooth from start to finish. Ignasi trusted us from day one and gave us complete freedom to propose ideas, and that shows in the result.

The starting point: two separate Webflow projects, one for Mexico and another living on a subdomain for Brazil. The goal: bring everything together into a single project with Webflow Localization, redesigning the whole site along the way.

‍

‍

We presented several concepts aligned with the company's vision and values, always respecting Cubbo's visual identity. Together with Ignasi we kept refining the direction until we landed on the final concept. From there, every page got approved with minimal changes. It's rare to work with a client who responds this fast and this clearly.

As soon as the Home was approved for dev, we started building in parallel while design wrapped up the secondary pages. We used GSAP and components from the Osmo Supply library to give the site the movement it needed.

‍

‍

‍

Under the hood, the heavy lifting: structuring the CMS to migrate every Case Study and Blog post from both Mexico (es-MX) and Brazil (pt-BR), setting up the 301 redirect plan with Cloudflare, and connecting the Sales forms to HubSpot to trigger the Slack workflows.

descripcion: Full website development for Wisable, an M&A firm, featuring a scalable architecture, property-driven dynamic content, multi-step forms, and GSAP animations.

resena.texto: We have been collaborating with treseiscero for more than a year now and the results have been great, helping us grow our relationship with the client. His immense webflow knowledge, availbility and constant pursuit for the best solution have been a key assets to the success of the project.
resena.cargo: Founder and Managing Director at Farco Studio

historia:
It was a pleasure to collaborate, once again, with the design team at Farco Studio, led by Brian, to develop the website for Wisable, an M&A firm that helps owners of small and medium-sized businesses across the U.S. sell their companies, while also connecting them with entrepreneurs interested in acquiring them.

The development was built with scalability in mind from the start, taking into account color changes and the different structures of each component. All content was also connected to properties, making it easy to update text, images, or videos.

Two multi-step forms were also developed: one an onboarding flow for buyers interested in joining the acquisition opportunities network, and another functioning as a Readiness Calculator that assesses whether a business is sufficiently prepared to be sold, concluding with a dynamic note and recommendations based on the result.

All of this, combined with the resulting pages and detailed GSAP animations, makes this project a complete, solid website built to scale over time.
